recs.stt: What adults lost when kids stopped playing in the street
recs.x:
at can help to reduce the negative impacts of cars - in the immediate area. Though if you build an area out of cul-de-sacs with no bike/pedestrian shortcuts, you end up not being able to practically get around without a car, so the area around the cul-de-sacs needs lots of car infrastructure. (Which is not so great if your kids are unlucky enough to live across a wide arterial from their friends from school.)

But ultimately yes, reducing through traffic can be a good thing, and there are ways to do that in cities too. There's a good video on this here: [link]
